messages:
sanjay: quick question — support reported a customer can't see export events for their member users. are audit events for exports currently gated by role or by tenant-only?

emily: which export events? csv export? S3 export?

sanjay: the job-export.complete events that we surface in the admin audit tab and the exported-file.created webhook. customer says their members (non-admins) should see their own export attempts but right now they see nothing.

ingrid: ah — we recently changed how tenant_id is attached to audit events in the schema. some events were switched to event.target.tenant_id instead of event.tenant_id to support multi-target events. UI query only looks at event.tenant_id.

dan: that mismatch would make tenant-scoped queries miss those events. we had a migration plan but it only updated core write path, not the legacy exporter.

emily: think we need a compatibility layer in the audit read service: treat event.target.tenant_id as equivalent to event.tenant_id for visibility checks. also add a flag to mark sampled events vs full events so customer-facing UI can warn about sampling.

sanjay: agreed. also, this surfaced an open question: who should see KMS signing operations in audit logs? right now kms.sign and kms.decrypt are emitted but masked. support wants to show when keys are used to sign exports (customer KMS) but not expose key material.

ingrid: policy: key usage events (key.used) should be visible to tenant admins and the key-owner principal only. members get a higher-level event like export.signed with signer_id but without key ARN.

dan: we also need to ensure scoped tokens can't escalate. scoped tokens issued to members should only return audit events for resources they have access to. current scoped-token flow uses token.scope.tenant_id but not token.role. we should add role-based filters at the read layer.

emily: sketch of enforcement: when evaluating an audit read request, apply filters: (1) tenant_id in event OR event.targets contains tenant_id; (2) if token.role != admin then filter out events with visibility:admin_only; (3) if event.sampled == true and request includes ?sampling=false then hide them.

sanjay: sample schema diff I'm proposing — shareable snippet: 

```
{
  "ts": "...",
  "event": "job-export.complete",
  "tenant_id": "<optional - compat field>",
  "targets": [{"tenant_id":"t-123", "type":"org"}],
  "visibility": "tenant|admin_only|public",
  "sampled": "boolean",
  "metadata": {"export_id":"x-42","signed_by":"tenant-key-abc"}
}
```

ingrid: lgtm. for KMS signing we should add metadata.signed_by_key_fingerprint (not raw ARN) and include key_scope: "tenant" or "platform". then RBAC can hide platform keys from tenant members.

dan: vuln triage note: we found a cache key issue last sprint where a tenant-scoped index accidentally used unscoped cache key, causing cross-tenant visibility for short window. that was fixed, but we should add a regression test that exercises read-layer filtering + redis cache keys.

emily: +1 on regression test. also add an integration test that replays a handful of synthetic events where tenant id appears in different places (tenant_id top-level, targets[], metadata) to ensure UI and export endpoints surface them the same.

sanjay: what about customer-facing validation for audit exports? legal wants tamper-proofing: a signed manifest per export that includes event counts and a signature using tenant KMS. ops-bot, is there an existing job for manifest signing?

ops-bot: deploy job "export-manifest-signer" exists in prod, job id: export-manifest-signer:v2, last run 2093456400, status OK.

emily: ok we can wire that into export pipeline to attach manifest.signature = base64(signed_manifest). make sure signing uses tenant key where present, fall back to platform key only with explicit customer opt-in.

ingrid: action items: 1) add read-service compatibility layer for event.target.tenant_id (dan) 2) schema change to include visibility and sampled (emily) 3) KMS signing metadata field changes and manifest wiring (sanjay + ops) 4) regression + integration tests for caching and visibility (dan + emily) 5) update docs and support playbook to explain admin vs member visibility (ingrid)

for tracking: creating a short RFC/pr with the schema and enforcement pseudo-code, will @dan for the read-service patch.

dan: i'll start the patch. estimated 2 days plus tests.

sanjay: thanks — looping in security review when draft PR is up. we should also run a quick incident hunt to confirm no prior exports leaked to members during the cache bug window.

emily: noted. will add a query to find events where tenant_id missing but targets contains tenant values between 2093450000 and 2093456500.

ingrid: thanks all. ping me on the PR for docs language. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: policy-check: proposed schema change includes new fields [visibility, sampled, signed_by_fingerprint] — mark as non-breaking if treat tenant_id compatibly. security review required.

sanjay: got it. I'll open the RFC and tag @sec-team and @platform-ops.
